positive: Select a local property from a method of its declaring class.

edge: Use a shadowed property name and verify object-class scope resolution.
negative: Pass an arbitrary expression rather than a property name.
positive: Select public and inherited accessible properties by name.

edge: Temporarily select a nonrandom property and verify it behaves as noncyclic random for that call only.
positive: Select a randc property in an argument list and verify its cyclic behavior remains.

edge: Temporarily exclude all but one rand property.
positive: Temporarily randomize an ordinary property and verify later no-argument calls revert to declared random variables.

edge: Declare unrelated helper methods with different names or signatures only where legal.
negative: Attempt to declare an overriding randomize method.
positive: Use the inherited built-in method.

edge: Call no-argument randomize on a class declaring no random variables.
positive: Use randomize(null) with currently satisfied and violated constraints and verify status without value changes.

edge: Verify retained objects participate in randomization.
positive: Grow a dynamic array of handles and verify new entries are null.

edge: Include nested active random objects.
positive: Initialize random members, force an unsatisfiable call, and verify all original values remain.

edge: Include an ordinary non-rand member.
notes: Do not rely on values changing by chance.
positive: Randomize an object with two rand members and make participation of both observable.

edge: Include nested active random objects.
negative: Use contradictory active hard constraints and require return value 0.
positive: Check for return value 1 on a satisfiable object.

edge: Use multiple active constraints and verify their conjunction.
positive: Constrain address low bits to zero and verify every successful result is aligned.

edge: Include both inherited and derived random members.
positive: Call randomize through a base-typed handle to a derived object and verify derived constraints apply.

edge: Refer to an inherited random member inline.
positive: Verify a successful result satisfies both class and inline constraints.
Use randomize() with as a conditional expression and as a subexpression in an assignment.

edge: Use empty optional parentheses where grammar permits.
negative: Use null or with(formals) in a nonmethod scope randomize call.
positive: Parse object randomize calls with a variable list, null, with formal identifiers, and an inline block.

edge: Use the same local identifier in distinct code blocks.
positive: Declare production identifiers and code-block locals in separate randsequence invocations and verify automatic per-invocation storage.

edge: Place break in a deeply nested production call without a loop.
positive: Execute break directly in a production and inside a nested loop, verifying randsequence exit versus loop-only exit.
Associate two comma-separated case values with one production.

edge: Exercise no-match cases both with and without a default.
positive: Use overlapping matching case expressions and verify the first declared match generates its production.

edge: Use a default item with and without its optional colon.
positive: Declare a randsequence case production with explicit items and an optional default.

negative: Declare two default items in one randsequence case production.
positive: Declare one default production item.

edge: Leave every alternative unweighted and verify equal weighting.
positive: Mix one unweighted alternative with an explicitly weighted alternative and treat the omitted weight as 1.

edge: Use nested nonterminals with code blocks at multiple expansion levels.
positive: Record code-block execution for a generated production stream.

edge: Use an optional start production, typed production ports, and weighted rule code block.
negative: Use an undeclared syntactic form in a production.
positive: Parse minimal and multi-production blocks exercising each major production alternative.

edge: Change state in generated production code and use it in a later condition.
negative: Use a condition that cannot be converted to Boolean.
positive: Exercise true and false conditions with and without an else production.

edge: Use separate rules with different occurrence counts.
positive: Use one returning occurrence and repeated occurrences, verifying scalar versus [1:N] array and ordering.

negative: Attempt a hierarchical reference to a variable declared inside a randsequence code block.
positive: Use a code-block local only within its anonymous scope.

edge: Use a production with only one alternative as a control.
notes: Do not require a particular finite selection sequence.
positive: Define multiple observable alternatives and verify each generated stream selects one complete alternative.

edge: Use a one-item terminal production.
positive: Define nested nonterminals with sequential items and verify terminal expansion order.

edge: Use multiple formal directions where production rules permit them.
negative: Pass arguments to a production whose declaration has no compatible formals.
positive: Declare typed formal arguments with defaults and invoke with explicit and omitted default arguments.

edge: Access both first and last indexed occurrences of a repeated production.
positive: Read a single production return by name and repeated returns by indexed production name in the triggering production's code block.

edge: Explicitly declare void.
negative: Return data from an implicitly void production.
positive: Declare integral and string return types and omit the type for a void production.

negative: Return an expression incompatible with the production's declared return type.
positive: Return an expression matching a production's declared nonvoid type.

edge: Shadow an outer variable with a formal.
negative: Reference the formal from a different production scope.
positive: Reference one formal from multiple alternative rules and nested code blocks of the production.

edge: Use three explicit nonzero weights with a common factor.
positive: Define two weighted alternatives and statistically verify their proportional selection.

edge: Join more than two production items.
negative: Accept an output that reverses items within one input sequence.
positive: Interleave two multi-item sequences and verify every output is an order-preserving shuffle.

edge: Contrast completion of all iterations without break.
positive: Execute break during a repeated production and verify no later randsequence production runs.

edge: Compute the count using a random system function.
negative: Use a negative or nonintegral repeat count.
positive: Repeat a production zero, one, and several times.

edge: Use a nonrecursive grammar and verify one finite expansion.
notes: Bound recursion in tests to guarantee termination.
positive: Use a bounded recursive alternative to produce repeated expansion.

edge: Return from the top-level production and verify its scope of abortion.
positive: Return from a nested production and verify its remaining items are skipped while the parent's following production runs.

edge: Read a later occurrence or later array element and treat the result as undefined rather than asserting a value.
positive: Read values from preceding production occurrences.

negative: Attempt to obtain static lifetime for a randsequence local without the required static prefix.
positive: Declare a code-block static variable with the explicit static prefix.

edge: Use a grammar containing one production.
negative: Name an undefined production.
positive: Run the same grammar with an explicit nonfirst top production and with no name.

edge: Use a weight that changes to zero before a later selection.
positive: Change a state variable used by a weight between selections of the same enclosing production and observe the changed eligible distribution.

negative: Use a negative or nonintegral production weight.
positive: Use zero and positive integral production weights.

edge: Shrink then regrow the collection.
positive: Disable a retained element, resize, and compare it with a newly added active element.

edge: Use local:: on a listed name.
positive: List one colliding object property while leaving another unlisted.

edge: Use an empty argument list as checker mode.
negative: Use an expression where the grammar requires variable identifiers.
positive: Call randomize(...) and std::randomize(...) with and without a with block.

negative: Use an unsatisfiable scope constraint and verify return status 0.
positive: Use satisfiable scope constraints and verify return status 1.

edge: Use a variable visible through lexical scope lookup.
positive: Randomize a local variable and an enclosing module variable together under a constraint.

negative: Use an empty argument list with a false inline constraint and verify status 0 without variable changes.
positive: Call std::randomize() with an empty argument list and a true inline constraint, verifying unchanged variables and status 1.

edge: Change which variables are listed across successive calls.
positive: List two locals as arguments and reference an unlisted task argument as state in the inline constraint.

notes: Use only a state string obtained from the same implementation's get_randstate().
positive: Capture an object's state, consume random values, restore the captured state, and verify the subsequent stream repeats.

edge: Use several conflicting soft constraints and verify priority determines survivors.
positive: Override a soft default with a conflicting hard inline constraint and require success satisfying the hard constraint.

edge: Use a soft relation involving multiple rand variables.
negative: Apply soft to a randc or nonrandom state variable.
positive: Apply soft to a rand variable.

edge: Alias one contained object through multiple rand handles and verify the latest handle determines its priority.
positive: Conflict soft constraints in two contained objects and verify the later handle wins.

edge: Use multiple levels of contained rand objects.
positive: Conflict a container soft constraint with one in a contained rand object and verify the container wins.

edge: Use multiple inheritance levels and verify nearer derived layers outrank all ancestors.
positive: Conflict a derived soft constraint with a differently named inherited soft constraint and verify the derived one wins.

edge: Place definitions far apart in the same legal scope.
positive: Reverse external-definition order relative to prototype order and verify prototype order controls conflicts.

edge: Iterate an array with descending index bounds and use defined iteration order.
positive: Generate mutually conflicting soft constraints across ordered foreach iterations and verify the latter iteration wins.

edge: Use multiple compatible hard constraints and retain all.
positive: Conflict hard and soft constraints and verify hard wins; conflict layered soft constraints and verify the later layer wins.

edge: Use a hard inline constraint, which also overrides soft class constraints by hard priority.
positive: Conflict an inline soft constraint with a class soft default and verify inline wins.

edge: Compare soft constraints in separate blocks whose block declaration order determines relative position.
positive: Declare two contradictory soft constraints in one block and verify the later expression prevails.

edge: Ensure the low-priority constraint is retained when the high-priority one is individually impossible.
positive: Create cases where both, only the high priority, only the low priority, and neither soft constraint can coexist with hard constraints.

edge: Create a cycle through three variables.
negative: Declare both a before b and b before a.
positive: Declare a chain solve a before b before c through separate ordering items.

edge: Order sizes of two random dynamic arrays.
positive: Use solve a.size before another rand variable with and without parentheses.

edge: Use size both with and without parentheses.
negative: Add parentheses to an ordinary variable primary.
positive: Order single and comma-list variables, including a scoped or hierarchical primary and array.size().

edge: Order an enum variable as an integral type.
negative: Order a random object handle directly.
positive: Order integral and real rand variables.

edge: Use a distribution-sensitive case where non-equivalent reordering would be observable and require specified probabilities.
positive: Use an earlier-fixed variable whose unique value permits internal reordering without changing results.

edge: Specify multiple ordering relations that form a partial rather than total order.
notes: Use a statistically robust oracle.
positive: Order a small selector before a much wider dependent data variable and statistically verify selector-first marginal selection.

edge: A disabled rand declaration remains a rand variable syntactically; apply detailed active-state semantics as appropriate.
negative: Name a nonrandom state variable.
positive: Order two rand variables.

negative: Use contradictory constraints and permit failure.
positive: Use a system with exactly one solution.

edge: Mix integer and packed-bit operands.
positive: Solve a power-of-two relation expressed with shifts.

edge: Reseed one object after consuming part of its stream.
positive: Seed two equivalent objects with the same value and verify their subsequent random behavior is reproducible.

edge: Declare ordinary and static blocks in the same class.
negative: Place static in a grammar position not admitted by the declaration.
positive: Declare static constraint c {...}.

edge: Contrast with a nonstatic constraint whose mode remains per object.
positive: Disable a static constraint through one object and verify it is disabled when randomizing another instance.

negative: Combine static with a dynamic override specifier.
positive: Declare a static constraint without override specifiers.

edge: Exercise static object initializers in two distinct containing instances.
positive: Create statically initialized class objects in a module or package and compare reproducible streams under the same initialization seed/order.

edge: Exercise static processes in separate module instances.
positive: Create static processes in a containing module or package and compare reproducible streams under unchanged initialization order.

edge: Contrast with per-instance mode of a nonstatic member.
positive: Disable a static rand member through one instance and verify it is inactive through another.

edge: Contrast with a nonstatic randc member whose cycle state is per instance.
positive: Alternate randomize() calls across two instances and verify their static randc member advances one shared cycle.

edge: Contrast with a nonstatic random member.
positive: Randomize alternating instances and verify all observe the same updated static rand member.

edge: Use different counts of random calls per thread while preserving each thread's own sequence.

edge: Use only a discarded soft size constraint.
positive: Randomize an unconstrained nonempty queue and verify unchanged size and randomized elements.

edge: Use an enum random member and ensure results remain in its declared value set.

positive: Randomize an unconstrained small integral rand member.

edge: Choose legal combinations whose marginal probabilities differ despite equal joint probabilities.

positive: Use a small constrained pair with an enumerable nonrectangular legal solution set and statistically test equal combination probabilities.

edge: Include array leaf elements in the group.
positive: Apply unique to several small integral variables and verify pairwise inequality.

edge: Use a multidimensional unpacked array with integral leaves.
negative: Use an expression that does not denote an admitted variable or array form.
positive: Use singular integral and real variables plus an unpacked-array slice with legal leaf type.

edge: Use one range-list item, which is syntactically valid but semantically ineffective.
negative: Omit braces or supply a general computed expression.
positive: Parse unique {a, b, array_slice} using permitted variables.

edge: Combine a singular variable with array leaves of equivalent type.
negative: Mix nonequivalent member types in one unique group.
positive: Use members with equivalent integral types.

edge: Apply unique to an empty array or slice.
positive: Randomize with unique containing one singular variable.

edge: Use an array whose group expansion would include a randc-qualified member if applicable.
negative: Include a randc variable.
positive: Use rand variables in unique.

edge: Leave several mutually constrained variables unordered.

positive: Order a before b while leaving c unordered and test c with the final selection set.

edge: Use a packed integral type as the leaf of nested unpacked dimensions.
positive: Apply unique to a multidimensional unpacked array and compare all scalar leaves.
